## 9.8 Sensitivity of the coprecipitation correction to σ

`SIGMA_P` is the single most consequential constant in this correction —
`p_coprec_ugL` is exactly linear in it — and the published estimates
cluster into two physically distinct classes rather than forming one
continuous range: field/river waters (0.055–0.095 µmol/m², River Frome,
River Windrush, the Waterston chalk aquifer) and idealised synthetic
Ca(HCO₃)₂ solutions (0.13–0.22 µmol/m²), which run 2–4× higher because
they lack the competing solutes (Mg, Fe, dissolved organic matter) that
occupy sorption sites in real water. `SIGMA_P` (§9.5) adopts the low end
of the field cluster — River Frome, 5.5e-8 mol/m² — following Cohen et
al. (2013)'s identical choice for a directly analogous karst stream;
this section carries the rest of the field cluster and the laboratory
ceiling forward as an explicit envelope rather than asserting the point
estimate as the only possibility.

```{r coprec-sigma-sensitivity}
# p_coprec_molL was built as delta_ca_molL * (SIGMA_P * N_AVOG * D_CALCITE) * h_adsorbed,
# so for fixed delta_ca and h it is exactly proportional to SIGMA_P: rescaling
# the already-computed p_coprec_ugL is equivalent to, and cheaper than,
# rebuilding the join for each candidate sigma.
SIGMA_SENS <- c(
  field_low   = 5.5e-8,  # River Frome (House et al. 1986a) -- ADOPTED, = SIGMA_P
  field_high  = 9.5e-8,  # Waterston chalk aquifer (House et al. 1986a), field cluster upper end
  lab_ceiling = 1.5e-7   # synthetic Ca(HCO3)2 (House & Donaldson 1986); Cohen et al. (2013)'s
                         # laboratory upper-bound comparison value
)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(SIGMA_SENS["field_low"]), SIGMA_P)))

coprec_sigma_sens <- btc_nutrients %>%
  filter(solute == "SRP", !is.na(p_coprec_ugL)) %>%
  select(event_id, sample_btc, p_coprec_ugL, conc_corr_ugL) %>%
  crossing(sigma_label = names(SIGMA_SENS)) %>%
  mutate(
    sigma_molm2       = SIGMA_SENS[sigma_label],
    p_coprec_ugL_sens = p_coprec_ugL * (sigma_molm2 / SIGMA_P),
    frac_of_srp_sens  = p_coprec_ugL_sens / conc_corr_ugL
  )

coprec_sigma_sens %>%
  group_by(event_id, sigma_label) %>%
  summarise(
    sigma_umolm2        = first(sigma_molm2) * 1e6,
    coprec_median_ugL   = median(p_coprec_ugL_sens, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_of_srp_median  = median(frac_of_srp_sens,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = event_id, names_from = sigma_label,
              values_from = c(coprec_median_ugL, frac_of_srp_median)) %>%
  arrange(event_id) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

write_csv(coprec_sigma_sens, here("data_derived", "coprec_sigma_sensitivity.csv"))

dict_coprec_sigma_sens <- tribble(
  ~column, ~unit, ~description,
  "sigma_label",       "-",      "field_low (adopted, River Frome) / field_high (Waterston aquifer) / lab_ceiling (synthetic solution)",
  "sigma_molm2",        "mol/m2", "SIGMA_P value used for this row, from SIGMA_SENS",
  "p_coprec_ugL_sens",  "ug/L",   "p_coprec_ugL rescaled to sigma_molm2; linear rescaling of the SIGMA_P-based value",
  "frac_of_srp_sens",   "-",      "p_coprec_ugL_sens / conc_corr_ugL, at this sigma"
)
write_csv(dict_coprec_sigma_sens,
          here("data_derived", "dictionary", "dict_coprec_sigma_sensitivity.csv"))
```

> **QAQC note.** This is the same check Cohen et al. (2013) ran on the
> Ichetucknee: moving from the field value to the laboratory ceiling
> should not be treated as a free parameter choice, because at the
> laboratory end `frac_of_srp` can approach or exceed unity — the point
> where the corrected series stops being a correction and becomes mostly
> model output (§9.5's QAQC note). Where `frac_of_srp_sens` stays small
> across the whole field-to-lab envelope, the choice of `SIGMA_P` cannot
> change a conclusion; where it diverges sharply between `field_low` and
> `lab_ceiling`, that divergence — not the point estimate — is what
> belongs in the manuscript, alongside the physical argument (§9.5) for
> why the field cluster is the appropriate class for a stream rather
> than a synthetic solution.

## 9.9 Event-level mass balance: does the correction respect the injected P mass?

`frac_of_srp` (§9.5) is a per-grab, concentration-domain ratio: at each
sampled instant, how large the correction is relative to the SRP
measured at that instant. The `median(frac_of_srp)` printed there is the
size of a *typical* correction, not the size of what the event actually
lost — it weighs every grab equally regardless of when it was taken or
how much water carried it, and `h_adsorbed` tracks phosphate speciation
(§9.2), so `p_coprec_ugL` rises and falls with SRP across the curve
while most events sample the tail more densely than the peak. A median
across grabs is therefore not a mass balance.

The mass-domain question — how much elemental P did coprecipitation
remove from the whole event, and is that plausible against the P
actually injected — needs a discharge-weighted integral over the sampled
curve, the same construction §6 already uses to get discharge from the
NaCl mass balance (`hydro_probe`'s `integral_Ct_mgLs`, `pracma::trapz`):

$$ m_{P,\mathrm{cop}} = Q \int_0^{T} C_{P,\mathrm{cop}}(t)\,dt
   \qquad
   m_{\mathrm{SRP}} = Q \int_0^{T} C_{\mathrm{corr}}(t)\,dt $$

with $Q$ the adopted event discharge (`discharge_Ls`, treated as steady
over the duration of a single slug event, matching §6's own convention)
and the integral taken by trapezoidal rule over the sampled
`time_since_release_s`. Two ratios follow:

$$ f_{\mathrm{mass}} = \frac{m_{P,\mathrm{cop}}}{m_{\mathrm{SRP}}}
   \qquad
   \%_{\mathrm{injectate}} = 100\,\frac{m_{P,\mathrm{cop}}}{m_{P,\mathrm{added}}} $$

`f_mass` is the mass-weighted analogue of `frac_of_srp` and is the
number to compare it against. `%_injectate` is an independent physical
check that does not use `conc_corr_ugL` at all — it asks what fraction
of the elemental P mass released at the addition point was removed by
coprecipitation before it passed the sampling station. `m_P,added`
converts the phosphate-salt mass on the field sheet (`added_mass_PO4_g`,
`molar_mass_P_nutrient`, `nutrient_addition_phosphate_data.csv`) to
elemental P using the same molar-mass ratio, not the salt mass itself.

`p_coprec_ugL` is integrated as measured, not clamped at zero: a
negative value is a real model output at `flag_delta_ca_neg` events (the
reach gained calcium — §9.5 already documents the model is not
parameterised for that direction), and clipping it would silently
overstate the correction there. `conc_corr_ugL` is clamped at zero in
its integral, matching the convention already used for `nacl_mgL_grab`
in §6 (a background-corrected concentration can dip slightly negative
from measurement noise around a zero baseline; a transported mass cannot
be physically negative).

```{r coprec-mass-balance}
p_added <- p_raw %>%
  distinct(stream, date, added_mass_PO4_g, molar_mass_P_nutrient)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(p_added[c("stream", "date")]))

coprec_mass_balance <- btc_nutrients %>%
  filter(solute == "SRP", !is.na(p_coprec_ugL)) %>%
  select(event_id, stream, date, time_since_release_s, conc_corr_ugL,
         p_coprec_ugL, flag_delta_ca_neg) %>%
  left_join(events %>% select(event_id, discharge_Ls, flag_discharge_invalid),
            by = "event_id") %>%
  left_join(p_added, by = c("stream", "date")) %>%
  arrange(event_id, time_since_release_s) %>%
  group_by(event_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n                      = n(),
    t_span_s               = diff(range(time_since_release_s, na.rm = TRUE)),
    discharge_Ls           = first(discharge_Ls),
    flag_discharge_invalid = first(flag_discharge_invalid),
    flag_delta_ca_neg      = first(flag_delta_ca_neg),
    # conc_corr_ugL can be NA on a grab even when p_coprec_ugL is
    # defined (a bad concentration reading does not stop the
    # geochemical calc, which does not use conc_corr_ugL at all).
    # A single NA in the window propagates through pmax()/trapz()
    # to NA for mass_srp_exported_ug and therefore frac_mass_coprec,
    # while mass_p_coprec_ug and pct_of_injectate_coprec (below) are
    # unaffected -- this flag names that asymmetry instead of
    # leaving it to be reverse-engineered from a bare NA.
    flag_conc_corr_na_in_window = anyNA(conc_corr_ugL),
    added_mass_PO4_g       = first(added_mass_PO4_g),
    molar_mass_P_nutrient  = first(molar_mass_P_nutrient),
    # discharge-weighted trapezoidal integral over the sampled curve; NA
    # where there are too few points to integrate or no valid discharge
    # (mirrors the guard already used for integral_Ct_mgLs in Sec. 6).
    mass_srp_exported_ug = if (n >= 3 && t_span_s > 0 && !is.na(discharge_Ls))
                             discharge_Ls *
                               pracma::trapz(time_since_release_s, pmax(conc_corr_ugL, 0))
                           else NA_real_,
    mass_p_coprec_ug     = if (n >= 3 && t_span_s > 0 && !is.na(discharge_Ls))
                             discharge_Ls *
                               pracma::trapz(time_since_release_s, p_coprec_ugL)
                           else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    frac_mass_coprec        = mass_p_coprec_ug / mass_srp_exported_ug,
    mass_P_added_g          = added_mass_PO4_g * (M_P / molar_mass_P_nutrient),
    pct_of_injectate_coprec = 100 * (mass_p_coprec_ug / 1e6) / mass_P_added_g,
    flag_insufficient_samples     = n < 3,
    flag_coprec_exceeds_injectate = !is.na(pct_of_injectate_coprec) &
                                     pct_of_injectate_coprec > 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(frac_mass_coprec))

coprec_mass_balance %>%
  select(event_id, n, discharge_Ls, frac_mass_coprec, pct_of_injectate_coprec,
         flag_delta_ca_neg, flag_discharge_invalid, flag_insufficient_samples,
         flag_coprec_exceeds_injectate, flag_conc_corr_na_in_window) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

write_csv(coprec_mass_balance, here("data_derived", "coprec_mass_balance.csv"))

dict_coprec_mass_balance <- tribble(
  ~column, ~unit, ~description,
  "event_id",                     "-",     "Event key",
  "n",                             "-",     "Number of SRP grabs with a defined p_coprec_ugL",
  "t_span_s",                      "s",     "Time span covered by those grabs; integration domain",
  "discharge_Ls",                  "L/s",   "Adopted event discharge (events$discharge_Ls), treated as steady over the event",
  "mass_srp_exported_ug",          "ug",    "discharge_Ls * trapz(time_since_release_s, pmax(conc_corr_ugL, 0)); background-corrected SRP mass transported past the station over the sampled window",
  "mass_p_coprec_ug",              "ug",    "discharge_Ls * trapz(time_since_release_s, p_coprec_ugL); P mass removed by coprecipitation over the sampled window. Not clamped at zero -- see prose",
  "frac_mass_coprec",              "-",     "mass_p_coprec_ug / mass_srp_exported_ug; mass-weighted, event-integrated analogue of the per-grab median frac_of_srp in Sec. 9.5",
  "added_mass_PO4_g",              "g",     "Mass of the phosphate salt added, nutrient_addition_phosphate_data.csv",
  "molar_mass_P_nutrient",         "g/mol", "Molar mass of the salt added (type_P)",
  "mass_P_added_g",                "g",     "added_mass_PO4_g * (M_P / molar_mass_P_nutrient); elemental P mass injected",
  "pct_of_injectate_coprec",       "%",     "100 * (mass_p_coprec_ug/1e6) / mass_P_added_g; independent check, does not use conc_corr_ugL",
  "flag_delta_ca_neg",             "-",     "Carried from Sec. 9.5: TRUE when the reach gained calcium (model not parameterised for that direction)",
  "flag_discharge_invalid",        "-",     "Carried from Sec. 6: TRUE when no valid discharge estimate exists for this event",
  "flag_insufficient_samples",     "-",     "TRUE when n < 3 (cannot integrate); mass columns are NA",
  "flag_coprec_exceeds_injectate", "-",     "TRUE when pct_of_injectate_coprec > 100 -- physically impossible, flags a remaining error rather than a real effect",
  "flag_conc_corr_na_in_window",   "-",     "TRUE when any conc_corr_ugL in the window is NA; frac_mass_coprec is then NA but pct_of_injectate_coprec (independent of conc_corr_ugL) is not -- expected, not a bug"
)

write_csv(dict_coprec_mass_balance,
          here("data_derived", "dictionary", "dict_coprec_mass_balance.csv"))

dict_coprec_mass_balance
```

> **QAQC note.** `frac_mass_coprec` is the number that should be
> compared to the per-grab median in §9.5, not treated as a replacement
> for it — a large gap between the two says the loss is concentrated in
> part of the curve the median under- or over-weights, which is itself
> worth reporting. `pct_of_injectate_coprec` is the stronger check: it
> is built from the addition record alone (`added_mass_PO4_g`,
> `molar_mass_P_nutrient`) and the coprecipitation model, with no
> dependence on the measured downstream SRP series, so it cannot inherit
> an error from `conc_corr_ugL`. Any
> `flag_coprec_exceeds_injectate == TRUE` means the model is predicting
> more P removed than was released — physically impossible — and should
> be read as evidence of a remaining unit or join error, not as a real
> effect, per the same standard applied to `SIGMA_P` and the PHREEQC
> unit fixes earlier in this section.
>
> `flag_conc_corr_na_in_window` explains the one asymmetric case:
> `frac_mass_coprec` can be `NA` while `pct_of_injectate_coprec` is not,
> because a single `NA` in `conc_corr_ugL` propagates through the
> `mass_srp_exported_ug` integral but `mass_p_coprec_ug` never uses
> `conc_corr_ugL` at all. This is expected behaviour, not a second bug.
>
> **A note on circularity.** `p_coprec_ugL` — and therefore
> `conc_corr_coprec_ugL` — is a deterministic function of `delta_ca_mgL`
> (§9.2). Any uptake metric computed from the corrected series (Sw, Vf,
> areal uptake, or otherwise) therefore carries a component that is
> mechanically linear in ΔCa by construction, independent of any real
> biological or abiotic process. Comparing that metric, once corrected,
> back against ΔCa or calcium transfer and reporting agreement as
> confirmation of the coprecipitation mechanism is circular — the
> correction was built from ΔCa, so some relationship between the two is
> guaranteed rather than discovered. The evidence that is not circular
> is the relationship measured on the *uncorrected* series (nothing in
> `conc_corr_ugL` depends on ΔCa) and the independent mass-balance check
> above (`pct_of_injectate_coprec`, built from the addition record, not
> from ΔCa or the corrected concentration). A relationship that is
> absent uncorrected and appears only after applying the correction is
> particularly worth treating with suspicion for this reason before
> being reported as a finding — it is at least as consistent with the
> correction's own linear structure as with a newly-revealed process.

# 10. Consolidated master dataset for inverse TSM

Earlier versions of this section built one dataset for the RA reach
only, and explicitly excluded 2023-10-05 (both stations) from it: that
day's SRP series is erratic (swings from -3 to +120 µg/L point to point,
no coherent rise-fall shape), a broken NaCl-nutrient pairing traced to
the same pre-tracer instrument step documented in Section 3, and not to
co-precipitation (`03` §1.1 shows the predicted correction is the same
negligible order for both RA dates). That exclusion contradicted this
project's own standing rule: quantify and flag uncertainty, never
silently drop a stream. **It is reversed here.**

This section now builds one master table across **every** event with a
nutrient series — nothing is dropped. Discharge and reach geometry come
from each event's own individually-adopted value in `events` (Section
6), \*\*with no override, including for RA_20230906_N/\_P\*\*: each
slug's own hydraulics (`water_velocity_ms`, `stream_depth_m`, and
whatever an inverse model derives from its own BTC) must stay internally
consistent with the same discharge that was used to derive them in
Section 6. As of Section 6's latest correction, `discharge_Ls` for
RA_20230906_N, RA_20230906_P, and RA_20231005_downstream is now the
probe (handheld trapezoidal) estimate rather than the manual Excel value
— each still carries its own individually-adopted number, not a shared
one. What the two RA_20230906 slugs' reach genuinely shares that day —
one physical river, one set of survey geometry — is a separate,
explicitly-labelled reference pair, `discharge_Ls_day_mean`/`_sd` (mean
and sd of the two slugs' own adopted `discharge_Ls`), populated only for
those two rows and not substituted into `discharge_Ls` anywhere. To make
the logger-vs-probe-vs-manual picture fully inspectable from this table
alone — not just from `events.csv` — the raw per-source estimates
(`discharge_Ls_logger`, `discharge_Ls_probe`, `discharge_Ls_manual`),
the adopted method, and the reason the logger was rejected where it was
are carried forward here too. Every known data-quality problem —
RA_20231005 upstream's incomplete mixing, RA_20231005's broken pairing
(both stations), missing baselines, a peak barely above background,
sparse recessions, discharge that could not be estimated at all — is
carried forward as an explicit flag column instead. Whether to use,
weight, or exclude a flagged event is a modelling decision made
downstream of this table, not a decision this pipeline makes on anyone's
behalf; RA_20231005_upstream in particular is expected to sit unused as
a reference row for now.

```{r ra-reach-discharge}
# Day-level reference discharge for the two RA 2023-09-06 slugs, ~2h15min
# apart, same physical reach. Built from each slug's own ADOPTED
# discharge_Ls in `events` -- not a hardcoded pair of numbers -- so this
# stays consistent automatically if Section 6's source decision for either
# slug ever changes again (it already has once: manual -> probe). This
# mean is NOT substituted into either event's own discharge_Ls below --
# each slug's own velocity/depth were derived from its own value, and
# overwriting it would break that internal consistency. It is instead
# kept as a day-level REFERENCE for what the river's discharge looked
# like that day (mean of two independent estimates of the same
# underlying flow, spread carried as uncertainty rather than picking
# one) -- available if a future step wants a single characterising Q
# for 2023-09-06, not used by this table itself.
ra_q_lookup <- events %>%
  filter(event_id %in% c("RA_20230906_N", "RA_20230906_P")) %>%
  select(event_id, discharge_Ls)

stopifnot(nrow(ra_q_lookup) == 2, !anyNA(ra_q_lookup$discharge_Ls))

RA_Q_VALUES   <- set_names(ra_q_lookup$discharge_Ls, ra_q_lookup$event_id)
RA_Q_MEAN_LS  <- mean(RA_Q_VALUES)
RA_Q_SD_LS    <- sd(RA_Q_VALUES)

tibble(discharge_Ls_mean = RA_Q_MEAN_LS, discharge_Ls_sd = RA_Q_SD_LS,
       cv_pct = 100 * RA_Q_SD_LS / RA_Q_MEAN_LS)
```

> **QAQC note.** `sd()` on two points is `abs(diff(x))/sqrt(2)` —
> reported here because it is the standard, honest way to carry a
> 2-value spread forward, not because n=2 supports a distributional
> claim. The mean/sd printed above is carried in the master table below
> as `discharge_Ls_day_mean`/`_sd`, a reference value only;
> `discharge_Ls` for RA_20230906_N and RA_20230906_P stays each slug's
> own adopted value, exactly as in `events`/`hydraulics`.

```{r master-tsm-export}
# Day-level reference discharge for RA 2023-09-06 only (see prose and
# QAQC note above) -- NA for every other event, including RA_20231005.
# Not used to compute discharge_Ls, water_velocity_ms, or stream_depth_m
# anywhere in this table.
ra_day_reference <- tibble(
  event_id                  = names(RA_Q_VALUES),
  discharge_Ls_day_mean     = RA_Q_MEAN_LS,
  discharge_Ls_day_mean_sd  = RA_Q_SD_LS
)

master_hydraulics <- events %>%
  select(event_id, discharge_Ls, reach_length_m, reach_mean_width_m,
         discharge_source, discharge_method, reason_discharge,
         discharge_Ls_logger, discharge_Ls_probe, discharge_Ls_manual,
         flag_discharge_invalid, flag_mixing_incomplete,
         flag_no_baseline, flag_weak_signal, flag_sparse_recession) %>%
  left_join(ra_day_reference, by = "event_id") %>%
  mutate(
    # RA 2023-10-05, both stations: erratic SRP series, broken NaCl
    # pairing (see prose above). NOT excluded -- flagged.
    # RA_20231005_downstream already carries flag_no_baseline == TRUE
    # (Section 6, contaminated start anchor) and RA_20231005_upstream
    # already carries flag_mixing_incomplete == TRUE; this flag is the
    # additional, independent problem with the nutrient pairing itself.
    flag_broken_pairing = event_id %in% c("RA_20231005_upstream",
                                          "RA_20231005_downstream")
  )

# guard: one hydraulics row per event, so the join below cannot
# multiply rows.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(master_hydraulics$event_id))

master_tsm <- btc_nutrients %>%
  left_join(master_hydraulics, by = "event_id") %>%
  arrange(event_id, solute, time_since_release_s)

# guard: every event in btc_nutrients survives the join (left_join
# cannot drop left-table rows, but a name/type mismatch could still
# silently produce all-NA hydraulics -- catch that here), and wherever
# discharge_Ls itself is NA, flag_discharge_invalid says so.
stopifnot(setequal(unique(master_tsm$event_id), unique(btc_nutrients$event_id)))
stopifnot(all(master_tsm$flag_discharge_invalid[is.na(master_tsm$discharge_Ls)]))

write_csv(master_tsm, here("data_derived", "master_tsm.csv"))
saveRDS(master_tsm,   here("data_derived", "master_tsm.rds"))

master_tsm %>%
  distinct(event_id, discharge_Ls, discharge_source, discharge_method,
           discharge_Ls_logger, discharge_Ls_probe, discharge_Ls_manual,
           discharge_Ls_day_mean, flag_discharge_invalid,
           flag_mixing_incomplete, flag_no_baseline, flag_weak_signal,
           flag_sparse_recession, flag_broken_pairing) %>%
  arrange(event_id) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

dict_master_tsm_extra <- tribble(
  ~column, ~unit, ~description,
  "discharge_Ls",             "L/s", "Adopted event discharge, taken straight from events$discharge_Ls with no override for any event -- source given by discharge_source/discharge_method",
  "reach_length_m",            "m",   "events$reach_length_m, unchanged for every event",
  "reach_mean_width_m",        "m",   "events$reach_mean_width_m, unchanged for every event",
  "discharge_source",          "-",   "logger / probe / manual_excel / NA, from events, unchanged for every event",
  "discharge_method",          "-",   "Method behind the adopted discharge_Ls (logger_trapz_truepeak / probe_trapz_endrising / manual_fixed_background)",
  "reason_discharge",          "-",   "Why the logger was not used, where it was not; NA when the logger is the adopted source",
  "discharge_Ls_logger",       "L/s", "Raw logger-based trapezoidal estimate (Sec. 6), independent of which source was adopted; NA where no usable logger series exists",
  "discharge_Ls_probe",        "L/s", "Raw handheld/probe-based trapezoidal estimate (Sec. 6), independent of which source was adopted; currently the adopted source for RA_20230906_N/_P and RA_20231005_downstream",
  "discharge_Ls_manual",       "L/s", "Manual Excel value (fixed background, negatives retained), Sec. 6; kept as reference only -- not the adopted source for any event as of this revision",
  "discharge_Ls_day_mean",     "L/s", "mean(each slug's own adopted discharge_Ls), RA_20230906_N/_P only; NA for every other event. A reference value for the river's discharge that day -- NOT used to compute discharge_Ls or anything derived from it in this table",
  "discharge_Ls_day_mean_sd",  "L/s", "sd() of the same two adopted values, RA_20230906_N/_P only; NA elsewhere",
  "flag_discharge_invalid",    "-",   "TRUE when no usable discharge exists for this event -- currently RA_20231005_upstream only",
  "flag_mixing_incomplete",    "-",   "TRUE for RA_20231005_upstream: logger sampled the plume core, not a well-mixed cross-section, so the dilution-gauging premise fails",
  "flag_no_baseline",          "-",   "TRUE when the window carries no clean pre-release baseline (RA_20230906_N, RA_20231005_downstream)",
  "flag_weak_signal",          "-",   "TRUE when the adopted trapezoidal estimate's peak is only marginally above background noise (RA_20230906_P: ~3%)",
  "flag_sparse_recession",     "-",   "TRUE when one unsampled interval holds >30% of the handheld trapezoidal area",
  "flag_broken_pairing",       "-",   "TRUE for RA_20231005 (both stations): SRP series is erratic (-3 to +120 ug/L point to point, no coherent shape) and the NaCl pairing is at or near zero for nearly the whole grab window, per Section 3 and 03 Sec 1.1. NOT excluded from this table -- using, weighting, or dropping these rows is a modelling decision, not a pipeline decision"
)
write_csv(bind_rows(dict_btc_nutrients, dict_coprec, dict_master_tsm_extra),
          here("data_derived", "dictionary", "dict_master_tsm.csv"))

nrow(master_tsm)
dict_master_tsm_extra
```

> **QAQC note.** This table replaces the RA-only `ra_reach_tsm` /
> `RA_reach_tsm.csv` from earlier versions of this section, which
> excluded RA_20231005 outright. Every event is here now, and
> `flag_broken_pairing`, `flag_discharge_invalid`,
> `flag_mixing_incomplete`, `flag_no_baseline`, and `flag_weak_signal`
> are how a modelling step should decide what to do with a given event,
> not something this pipeline decides on its behalf.
> RA_20231005_upstream in particular is expected to sit unused, as a
> reference row, until there is a specific reason to touch it.
> `discharge_Ls_logger`/`_probe`/`_manual` are all carried here (not
> just `discharge_Ls`) specifically so this table alone supports a
> source-vs-source comparison — see the 1:1 plot in Section 6 for the
> logger-vs-probe picture across all events. Running the inverse model
> on all events, dropping the flagged ones, or running a sensitivity
> comparison with/without them is a choice for whichever conversation
> builds that model next (see the handoff).
